content.title: Hidden Poison: Machine unlearning enables camouflaged poisoning attacks
content.abstract: We introduce camouflaged data poisoning attacks, a new attack vector that arises in the context of machine unlearning and other settings when model retraining may be induced. An adversary first adds a few carefully crafted points to the training dataset such that the impact on the model's predictions is minimal. The adversary subsequently triggers a request to remove a subset of the introduced points at which point the attack is unleashed and the model's predictions are negatively affected. In particular, we consider clean-label targeted attacks (in which the goal is to cause the model to misclassify a specific test point) on datasets including CIFAR-10,  Imagenette, and Imagewoof. This attack is realized by constructing camouflage datapoints that mask the effect of a  poisoned dataset.
